newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Pessimism in N.Irish hotel industry rises - survey.
newsitem.headline: Pessimism in N.Irish hotel industry rises - survey.

text.p: Pessimism in the Northern Irish hotel industry increased in the last quarter of 1996 as the slow pace of the peace process hit confidence, a survey showed.

The survey, carried out by BDO Stoy Hayward in the quarter from October to December 1996, found that 34 percent of respondents felt pessimistic about the outlook for the next three months compared with 17 percent in the previous quarter and four percent in the same period of 1995.
BDO Stoy Hayward said much of the pessimism may be attributed to the poor performance experienced toward the end of last year.
Of those surveyed, 47 percent said revenues in the last quarter of 1996 were down on the previous year, while 75 percent reported similar or lower occupancy than in the same period of 1995.

But the survey also found that 97 percent of hoteliers intended maintaining or increasing expenditure on training in the next three months, while 74 percent expected to maintain or increase staff numbers.
"Northern Ireland hoteliers continue to operate in a difficult market place given the state of the peace process," Shaun Kelly, partner in charge of tourism at BDO, said.

He said there had been an overwhelming response to Brand Ireland, the joint marketing initiative launched by Bord Failte, the Irish tourist board, and the Northern Irish Tourist Board, late last year.

"However, this was tempered by many respondents who believe that until such time as we have a peaceful environment in Northern Ireland, the industry will not fully reap the benefits of such an initiative," Kelly said.
The IRA ended a 17-month ceasefire on February 9, 1996 by bombing London's Canary Wharf and has attacked security targets in Northern Ireland since last October.
